speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help diagnose the cause of your bleeding and petechiae, how old are you, and have you noticed any joint pain or swelling?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the child had any recent illnesses, vaccinations, or exposure to new medications? I also need to know if there is any family history of bleeding disorders.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_platelet_count
REQUEST TEST: Coagulation_panel_(PT_PTT)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count (CBC): WBC 6,500 /μL, Hemoglobin 12.1 g/dL, Platelets 280,000 /μL (normal). Coagulation Panel: PT 12 seconds (normal), aPTT 30 seconds (normal). Peripheral Blood Smear: No clumping of platelets observed, normal morphology of other cells. Special Test (ELISA Binding Assay): Platelet surfaces deficient in GIIb/IIIa receptors.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal platelet count and coagulation studies, combined with the specific deficiency in GIIb/IIIa receptors, point to a platelet function disorder rather than a quantity issue. This specific receptor defect is characteristic of Glanzmann thrombasthenia. DIAGNOSIS READY: Glanzmann thrombasthenia
